text: So there are sort of three technologies that are really important for helping build a mental model of the tool and how it works, how it works and why it works.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So the first one is that everything is mocked out.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So at record time, we record all the network requests and responses.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And then at replay time, we stub those in.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And we perform that mocking for two reasons.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: One is to make the test idempotent so you can run them 1,000 times in a row and get the same results each and every time.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And the second reason is it means that every test is isolated from every other test, which eliminates the risk of race conditions and allows you to paralyze the test horizontally and get the results in a few minutes.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The second key technology is that you get radically less or orders of magnitude less flakes with Meticulous than any other tool, including Cypress or Playwright.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And the reason why is we augment the browser from the scheduling engine layer up to be fully deterministic.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So when browsers were first designed, determinism was not a design goal.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so there's many different sources of randomness.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: For instance, an animation spinner depends upon the clock speeds of the CPU or the machine rendering the browser or the interleaving between set timeout and set interval.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so we handle all of that randomness and make the browser deterministic or near deterministic so that you have radically, radically less flakes.

text: And then the third technology, which is the most important one for grokking, like why this works, is if you want this to be exhaustive, it has to cover every feature-flang combination, every permission, every role, every config, every possible branching through the application.
